title: Fixtures and test lifetime
summary: A new test-class instance per test, constructor and Dispose as setup and teardown, IClassFixture and collection fixtures for expensive things, IAsyncLifetime for async setup, ITestOutputHelper for diagnostics.

steps.title: xUnit makes a new object for every test
body: xUnit has no `[SetUp]` attribute. It creates a **new instance of the test class for every test**, so the constructor is the setup and `Dispose` (or `DisposeAsync`) is the teardown:
```csharp
public class CartTests : IDisposable
readonly Cart cart = new();          // fresh for every test: no test sees another's items
public CartTests() => cart.Add("mug", 8.00m);
[Fact] public void Starts_with_one_item() => Assert.Single(cart.Items);
[Fact] public void Clear_empties_it() { cart.Clear(); Assert.Empty(cart.Items); }
public void Dispose() { /* runs after each test */ }

This is deliberate isolation: instance fields cannot leak between tests, in any order. The only way to share state is to ask for it explicitly, and **static** fields, which bypass all of this and are the classic cause of tests that pass alone and fail together.

steps.prompt: A class has 3 `[Fact]`s and a `[Theory]` with 4 `[InlineData]` rows. How many times does its constructor run in one test run?
steps.explain: One instance per test case, and every theory row is a test case: 3 + 4 = 7. That is why an expensive setup does not belong in the constructor.

steps.title: Sharing expensive things on purpose: fixtures
body: Some setup is too slow to repeat for every test: starting a web host, creating a database, loading a big file. A **fixture** is created once and handed to the tests that ask for it:
```csharp
public sealed class DatabaseFixture : IAsyncLifetime
public PriceDb Db { get; private set; } = null!;
public async ValueTask InitializeAsync() => Db = await PriceDb.OpenAsync();   // once, before the first test
public async ValueTask DisposeAsync() => await Db.DisposeAsync();           // once, after the last
public class PriceTests(DatabaseFixture fixture, ITestOutputHelper output) : IClassFixture<DatabaseFixture>
[Fact]
public void Mugs_cost_eight()
output.WriteLine("checking the mug price");   // shown with this test's result
Assert.Equal(8.00m, fixture.Db.PriceOf("mug"));
| Scope | How | Shared by |
| one test class | `IClassFixture<T>` on the class, `T` in the constructor | the tests of that class |

| several classes | `[CollectionDefinition("db")] class DbCollection : ICollectionFixture<T>;` and `[Collection("db")]` on each class | every class in the collection (and they no longer run in parallel with each other) |
| the whole assembly | `[assembly: AssemblyFixture(typeof(T))]` | every test (new in v3) |

In v3 `IAsyncLifetime` returns `ValueTask` and extends `IAsyncDisposable`. `ITestOutputHelper` (now in the `Xunit` namespace) is injected the same way, and `TestContext.Current` gives the current test, its cancellation token and a key-value store from anywhere.
Shared fixtures must be **read-only** for the tests, or tests start depending on each other's leftovers.

steps.prompt: A class uses `IClassFixture<DatabaseFixture>` and has two tests, A then B. Put what xUnit does in order.
lines: new PriceTests(fixture), run test A, Dispose it
new PriceTests(fixture), run test B, Dispose it
steps.explain: The fixture lives across the class; the test-class instance is still new for every test. That is the whole design: share the expensive, isolate the rest.

steps.prompt: Where does each piece of setup belong?
items: a fresh `Cart` to add items to
a SQLite database with the schema created
an order builder with default values
steps.explain: Cheap, mutable things are built per test so tests cannot affect each other. Slow things that tests only read go in a fixture.

steps.title: Open the expensive thing once
prompt: `PriceDb` is slow to open, so it refuses to be opened twice in one test run. It is compiled beside your tests:
throw new InvalidOperationException("PriceDb is expensive: open it once in a fixture, not in every test.");
public decimal PriceOf(string sku) => prices.TryGetValue(sku, out var p) ? p : throw new KeyNotFoundException(sku);
public decimal Basket(params string[] skus) => skus.Sum(PriceOf);
1. `public sealed class PriceDbFixture : IAsyncLifetime` with a `PriceDb Db` property, opened in `InitializeAsync` and disposed in `DisposeAsync`;

2. `public class PriceTests` that uses it through `IClassFixture<PriceDbFixture>`, with at least **four** tests (prices, an unknown SKU, a basket). Take an `ITestOutputHelper` too and write one line from a test.
Opening the database in each test (or in the constructor) fails from the second test on.
starter: public PriceDb Db { get; private set; } = null!;
public ValueTask InitializeAsync() => throw new NotImplementedException();
public ValueTask DisposeAsync() => throw new NotImplementedException();
solution: public PriceDb Db { get; private set; } = null!;
public async ValueTask InitializeAsync() => Db = await PriceDb.OpenAsync();
public async ValueTask DisposeAsync() => await Db.DisposeAsync();
public class PriceTests(PriceDbFixture fixture, ITestOutputHelper output) : IClassFixture<PriceDbFixture>
public static TheoryData<string, decimal> Prices => new() { { "mug", 8.00m }, { "tea", 4.50m }, { "pot", 24.00m } };
public void Known_prices(string sku, decimal expected)

target: throw new InvalidOperationException("PriceDb is expensive: open it once in a fixture, not in every test.");
public decimal PriceOf(string sku) => prices.TryGetValue(sku, out var p) ? p : throw new KeyNotFoundException(sku);
public decimal Basket(params string[] skus) => skus.Sum(PriceOf);

mutants.name: the basket drops its first item

hints: `public async ValueTask InitializeAsync() => Db = await PriceDb.OpenAsync();`
The test class takes the fixture in its constructor: `public class PriceTests(PriceDbFixture fixture, ITestOutputHelper output) : IClassFixture<PriceDbFixture>`.
Check the basket with all three items (36.50) so a dropped first or missing item shows.
steps.explain: The fixture opens the database once for the whole class, and every test still gets its own `PriceTests` instance. Real suites use the same shape for a test web host or a database container.
